summary: 3 HIGH, 7 MEDIUM, 5 NIT. Shape, fence and stage decomposition are sound: I6 and I17 hold, the policy table is declared data over frozen classes/floors/ceilings/permanent, the record differs from an autonomous apply by one field, registerApplier is the extension point with proposals.cjs sha-asserted unchanged, and blast radius is computed part by part with a stated limit per part. Blocking: FR-14's 'unreachable by any proposal' is measurably false (timeline.cjs's SELF_MODIFY applier writes changes[].path verbatim and shared/autonomy-policy.json is not protected); the only reachable EDITS entry reads row.target, which does not exist on a dependencyAdvisor row; and lift() never clears autonomy.stopped.json, so an engaged halt cannot be undone in-app and criterion 22a contradicts isHalted().

findings.title: FR-14's "the STOP and the policy table are unreachable by any proposal" is false, and the argument given for it is the wrong argument
findings.where: FR-14, FR-13a, §E.2.2, §E.10 row "The policy's own authority", §I.2
findings.problem: Measured: loyaltyGuard.PROTECTED_FILES (electron/lib/loyaltyGuard.cjs:64-72) lists exactly seven paths and does not include shared/autonomy-policy.json, and inspectChanges applies no root confinement — so a hand-built proposal naming the policy data file passes assertChangesSafe at creation. Separately, electron/ipc/timeline.cjs:195-210 registers the pre-existing SELF_MODIFY applier whose body is fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(change.path)) + fs.writeFileSync(change.path, change.content) plus fs.rmSync for deletes, with no resolve-then-compare, no root check and no lstat — so an absolute path is written wherever the process can write, including <userData>/rama/autonomy.allow. The design's premise that the stop's state is unnameable because changes[].path cannot address a file outside the repo root is a property of this design's own applier, not of the system. The design closes both routes only for kind 'self-upgrade'.
findings.fix: Three parts. (a) Restate FR-14 with its real scope: unreachable by THIS design's proposer and applier, NOT by every proposal, naming timeline.cjs:199-207 and the fact that shared/autonomy-policy.json is unprotected. (b) Add criterion 19c: plant a kind 'self-modify' proposal naming shared/autonomy-policy.json and an absolute path to the allow-file, assert proposals.create accepts both today, and PRINT the residual rather than leaving it to prose. (c) Widen §I.2's ask to master to include shared/autonomy-policy.json in PROTECTED_FILES and the tripwire manifest, and offer the cheap mechanical close as master's decision: timeline.cjs is NOT a protected file, so applying §E.9's resolve-then-compare + lstat rule inside that applier and refusing action 'delete' is available — as a declared 20th changed file, raised in Part I rather than left to implementer discretion.

findings.title: The only reachable EDITS entry reads a field that does not exist on a dependencyAdvisor row
findings.problem: The adapter is (row) => ({editId:'pin-version', params:{name: row.name, version: row.target}}). Measured, dependencyAdvisor.assess() returns {name, pinned, latest, jump, jumpWhy, sensitive, security, diskDeltaBytes, signals, concerns, recommend, urgency, meaning} (electron/lib/dependencyAdvisor.cjs:189-205) and review() maps assess over its entries (:241-248). There is no 'target' field. So params.version is undefined, pin-version's no-range precondition is evaluated against undefined, and the single edit the loop can author either throws or writes "name": "undefined" into package.json. The headline claim 'today this loop can author exactly one kind of change' is unreachable as written, and criterion 41's diff assertion could only pass against a fixture carrying a field production never produces.
findings.fix: Use the measured field and handle the two states that must not pin: dependencyAdvisor: (row) => (row.jump === 'current' || row.jump === 'downgrade' || !row.latest ? null : {editId:'pin-version', params:{name: row.name, version: row.latest}}). jump === 'downgrade' must yield null because buildMeaning reads that state as 'the release was withdrawn, so this needs looking at rather than upgrading'. Extend criterion 90a to assert every ADAPTERS output names only fields present on a real assess() return, built from a registrySources.collect fixture.

findings.title: lift() does not clear the stopped-record, so an engaged halt cannot be undone in-app and criterion 22a contradicts isHalted()
findings.problem: isHalted() is presence-based (fs.accessSync(stoppedRecordPath()) => true) and engage() writes that record; nothing in the document ever deletes it. lift() is specified only as the writer of allowed:true. So after any engage — tray, env, or the automatic one on a fatal revert — a successful lift() leaves isHalted() true, and refreshScheduler.runNow, selfCare.runHealthSweep, marketIntel.tickResolveOutcomes and tickSyncNews all carry in-function isHalted() checks and stay no-ops. Criterion 22a's 'startAudit() re-arms it on lift' is satisfiable only for the one dispatcher with no in-function check, so a lift resumes one of five behaviours while the panel, reading the still-present record, keeps reporting them halted. lift() is also never specified to call refreshScheduler.start(), startSweep() or startScheduler(), so the resume path is asymmetric with engage()'s teardown and the asymmetry is undeclared. The tray 'Resume' item therefore cannot undo what the tray engaged, even once master adds system.suspend-autonomy.
findings.fix: Specify the resume and assert it, mirroring engage()'s ordering rule: lift(user, note) writes the allow-file FIRST, THEN unlinks <userData>/rama/autonomy.stopped.json, THEN calls refreshScheduler.start(), metaCognition.startAudit(), selfCare.startSweep(), marketIntel.startScheduler() — and declares that agents and sandbox children are NOT respawned, with the reason. Order 1-before-2 so a crash leaves 'allowed but still halted', the recoverable direction. Extend criterion 22d with a sixth state: after lift(), isHalted() is false, the stopped-record is gone, counting fakes prove runNow('ollama-catalog') calls task.run() and runHealthSweep() calls checkInstanceFailover again, and statusText() names all four as running; a planted mutation removing the unlink turns the row RED. If master prefers a halt be undoable only by hand, that is a valid answer — but then the tray 'Resume' item and criterion 22a's re-arm sentence must both go, and the choice belongs in Part I.

findings.title: pin-version edits package.json and never package-lock.json, and nothing in the plan can see the divergence
findings.where: §E.4.2a EDITS table; §E.1.2 class 6 ("package.json / package-lock.json diffs"); §E.5.2 plan table
findings.problem: The class is defined over both files; the transform touches one. A changed pin without the matching lockfile entry makes npm ci fail, and the verification plan for this change is JSON.parse plus a dependency-count row because node --check is meaningless for JSON. So the one authorable change is the one whose failure mode the plan is structurally unable to detect, in a tree where §124 already measured that an offline rebuild is impossible.
findings.fix: Pick one and write it into the table with the reason. (a) Recommended: changes[] stays length one over package.json and the weighing carries a mandatory con — 'package-lock.json is not updated by this change; npm ci will refuse until the lockfile is regenerated on the build machine' — with verdict needs-master-decision whenever the package is in dependencyAdvisor.SENSITIVE or a lockfile exists on disk. (b) Add a lockfile-sync precondition refusing pin-version while package-lock.json exists, which makes the edit unreachable in this repository and should be said rather than discovered. Either way add a criterion asserting the changes[] paths and the presence of the lockfile con.

findings.title: NOTICE's suite sensor is unspecified in four ways, including a prose parse the design forbids elsewhere
findings.problem: Four decisions are missing from a sensor that spawns processes and feeds a fingerprint: which suites (18 files match scripts/verify*.cjs in this worktree); whether admission is one admit() per sweep or per spawn (ADMISSION declares a single 128 MB label described as 'a spawned Node process', singular); the per-suite timeout (specified for verification steps and for nothing in NOTICE); and how 'the failing row name' is extracted. The house suites print '    PASS  <msg>' / '    FAIL  <msg>' under a '\n  <id> — <title>' header (scripts/verifyInvariants.cjs:66-73) and nothing declares that shape as a contract — so the measurement field is parsed out of free-form stdout, which is what FR-56 forbids for remedies, and a misparse silently changes the one value deduplication depends on.
findings.fix: Declare the sensor as frozen data the way ADAPTERS is declared: SUITE_SENSOR = {suites:['verifyInvariants.cjs','verifyLoyaltyTripwire.cjs'], rowPattern:/^\s*FAIL\s{2}(.+?)\s*$/m, sectionPattern:/^\s{2}(\S+)\s+—\s+(.+)$/m, timeoutMs:120000, admitPerSuite:true}, with field = '<id>/<row>'. State the two refusals: a suite exiting non-zero whose stdout matches no FAIL row yields sensorsAbsent['suite:<name>'] and NO finding (unchecked is not a finding), and a timeout is sensorsAbsent, never a suite-red finding. Add to criterion 26 a fixture of real captured suite stdout with two failing rows, asserting two findings with distinct fingerprints.

findings.title: meta.autonomy has two incompatible shapes, and it is the field the "no schema change" claim rests on
findings.where: §E.3 (autonomy: {appliedBy, autonomousApply}) versus §E.5.0 check 0 and §E.5.1a (meta.autonomy = {flag, recordedAt}); FR-54; criterion 83a; §E.9's opts row
findings.problem: Implemented as written the applier overwrites meta.autonomy, destroying appliedBy and autonomousApply — the two fields the forward-compatibility argument and the audit trail both depend on. FR-54, criterion 83a and §E.9 all say 'recorded into meta.autonomy' without naming a shape, so neither reading is privileged and a coder picks.
findings.fix: One shape carrying both facts, merged not assigned. Declare in §E.3: autonomy: {appliedBy:'master'|'rama', autonomousApply:false, flagFromOpts:false, recordedAt:'<ISO>'}. In §E.5.0 check 0: meta.autonomy = {...(meta.autonomy||{}), appliedBy:'master', flagFromOpts: opts?.autonomous === true, recordedAt: now}. Keeping the received flag under its own key is what makes 'what the caller claimed' and 'what the system decided' two auditable facts — collapsing them is how the renderer-supplied flag got mistaken for a gate. Extend criterion 83a to assert appliedBy and autonomousApply survive an apply.

findings.title: Criterion 25 asserts a measurement.source field the schema does not define
findings.problem: Three places define measurement as {sensor, field, value, at} and notice() is specified to throw on a malformed one; criterion 25 asserts a fifth field, measurement.source. Either the validator rejects what the criterion requires or the schema is wrong, and the suite is what decides — so it surfaces as a red row rather than a decision.
findings.fix: Restate criterion 25 in the declared vocabulary: '... yields exactly one finding, whose measurement.sensor is "selfModel.limits" and whose measurement.field is "fixable", and whose remedy is null BY DECLARATION (§E.4.1's ADAPTERS)'. If a provenance string genuinely adds something over sensor + field, add 'source' to §E.3, §E.9 and criterion 23 together — but ADAPTERS already owns that mapping, so it does not.

findings.title: The halted skip inside refreshScheduler.runNow has an unspecified interaction with the state it writes
findings.where: FR-12 and §E.2.5 ("isHalted() check before await task.run()", line 133) against refreshScheduler.cjs:125-159
findings.problem: runNow is also the recorder: every path writes state[name] = {lastRunAt, lastOk, failures, ...} then writeState(state), and status() derives lastRunAt, failures, nextDueAt, overdue, backingOff and staleness from it. The design says where the check goes and not what it does to the record. A halted skip recording lastOk:true makes the task look freshly run and not overdue — a label lying about work that did not happen, in the scheduler's own status surface; one recording ok:false inflates failures and drives the x2-to-x32 backoff so that lifting the halt leaves the task artificially deferred.
findings.fix: Specify the third outcome and assert it: runNow returns {ok:false, halted:true, reason} BEFORE readState(), touching no state, so a halt neither refreshes lastRunAt nor increments failures and status() keeps reporting the real staleness and backoff. Criterion 22a gains an eleventh assertion: with the halt engaged, runNow('ollama-catalog') leaves the persisted task state byte-identical.

findings.title: The two renderer surfaces are specified as new PAGES entries but have no component files, no loaders, and no host file in the changed-file table
findings.where: §E.0.1 ("two new PAGES entries"; registry.js changed; Evolution.jsx changed) and §E.12
findings.problem: Measured, a PAGES entry is half a page: registry.js holds a parallel LOADERS map of import('@pages/<X>/<X>.jsx'), lazyFor(id) returns null without one, routablePages() filters them out, and registryIssues() reports 'page "<id>" has no loader' (src/config/registry.js:255-309). The design declares two new entries with no new .jsx file, no LOADERS additions, and no change to src/pages/Settings/Settings.jsx — so the Autonomy panel has no host file at all. As written the work either produces two registry issues or the surfaces are panels inside existing pages, needing no PAGES entries and a Settings.jsx row in the file table. Separately, PAGES entries carry minTier plus a descriptive free-text capabilities[] array, NOT matrix keys, so §E.12's 'both at tiers the matrix already defines' conflates minTier with shared/capabilities.json — which matters because §E.13 asks master to add autonomy.view and the panel must gate on it itself.
findings.fix: Take the panel reading §E.12 actually describes: delete 'two new PAGES entries' and the I7 claim, leave src/config/registry.js UNCHANGED, add src/pages/Settings/Settings.jsx to the changed-file table ('a new Autonomy panel, gated on autonomy.view with the §E.13 degradation text when the capability is absent'), keep Evolution.jsx, and restate the tier sentence as 'both render inside pages the registry already defines at their existing minTier; the Autonomy panel additionally gates on autonomy.view, which is not in the matrix, so until master adds it the panel renders the §E.13 sentence and nothing else'. If master wants real pages instead, the file table needs two .jsx files, two LOADERS entries, two PAGES entries with ids/routes/minTier and a criterion asserting registryIssues() is empty — a bigger change than §E.0.1's 'nothing else changes', so master's call.

findings.title: FR-28 requires the plan to be re-run after a revert; no section implements it and no outcome is defined for a post-revert failure
findings.where: FR-28 against §E.5.2a's verdict object, §E.5.3's flow, §E.5.5's fatal case and §E.8 rows 20-22
findings.problem: The verdict object is {verified, reverted, revertAttested, causeId, cause, remedy, plan, planDrift, snapshotDir} — no field for a second plan run; §E.5.3 goes straight from failure to naming a cause; §E.5.5's fatal branch is reached only by a digest mismatch. So FR-28's third clause is unimplemented and the state it exists to detect has no handling: if the plan still fails after a successful, digest-attested revert, the tree was already red before the apply, the causeId attributed to this change is wrong, and §E.5.4 would file a corrected proposal chasing a defect the apply did not cause.
findings.fix: Name the step, the field and the outcome. revert(token) is followed by ONE re-run of the SAME re-derived plan. The verdict gains postRevertVerified: true|false|'not-run', with 'not-run' declared so it never renders as 'passed' (§E.5.2's needed/run rule). postRevertVerified:false => causeId 'pre-existing-red', confident:false, NO corrected proposal, and a question carrying both runs' evidence ('the tree did not verify before this change either') — the fourteenth id, in unrecognised-exit's confident:false precedent. Criterion 46 gains the fixture: an already-red temp repo, a clean revert, and assertions on postRevertVerified:false, causeId 'pre-existing-red', and that nothing was re-proposed.

findings.title: §B.3's "nine derivations ... seven of the nine" is eight
findings.problem: Measured: electron/lib/selfModel.cjs contains eight limit(...) calls (lines 210, 216, 222, 228, 241, 248, 255, 263), seven with a non-null fixable (the nucleus one has none).
findings.fix: Read: 'Eight derivations exist today ... fixable is a non-null string on seven of the eight.' The design's conclusions are unaffected — ADAPTERS declares null for this sensor by decision — but the inventory is what later sessions trust.

findings.title: Three stale line citations, one of them the kind revision pass 3 corrected elsewhere
findings.problem: §H.23 still reads 'agent.killFn at 634' while §E.2.5, §E.0.1 and §H.28 say 637 and explain why 634 pointed at a different caller (measured: killFn at 122, 140, 359, 637). proposals.cjs's authorise(opts.user, 'self-modify.apply') is at 219, not 215. The proposals:apply IPC handler is at 269, not 272. (applier(p, opts) at 235 and preload.cjs 680 are both correct.)
findings.fix: Fix the three citations. The 634 one matters most: a coder reading Part H first copies the wrong line, which is review-3 finding 17's failure mode surviving in the section that records it.

findings.title: "25 suites" is unsourced; the tree has 18 scripts/verify*.cjs
findings.problem: Measured: 18 files match scripts/verify*.cjs in this worktree; Section 124 recorded '22 JS suites' across the tree. Neither is 25, and this number lands in the master spec where it becomes the next session's baseline.
findings.fix: Say '18 scripts/verify* suites' or cite §124's 22 with its scope.

findings.title: §B.5's inventory row still says "four outbound paths", omitting evolutionEngine
findings.problem: That row describes 'Four outbound paths carrying text' while §E.0.1, §E.7.4, FR-33 and §I.8 all carry the corrected count — five files, seven paths, ten request sites, with evolutionEngine named as the fifth. Part B is read first.
findings.fix: Add evolutionEngine.cjs to the row's file list and change 'Four' to 'Seven paths across five files (§E.7.4 counts them; criterion 54a asserts the count)'.

findings.title: §E.0.1 places codeRegenEngine's gate call at a line that describes one of its three requests
findings.problem: §E.0.1 says 'before researchFix's DuckDuckGo URL at ~49' while §E.7.4 correctly says 'top of researchFix ~44' covering 49, 69 and 87 (DDG, npm registry, GitHub search — all three measured at those lines). Placing it at 49 happens to precede all three in the same function, so behaviour survives, but the file table should match the gate table.
findings.fix: Read: 'at the top of researchFix (~44), covering its three requests at 49, 69 and 87'.

verifiedAssumptions: proposals.cjs:235 calls applier(p, opts) with two arguments — FR-57's closure + exported applyWith is the only available seam

proposals.apply authorises opts.user before the applier runs (:219), so the applier's masterDriven derivation is tautologically true there — the design's move to criterion 21c's asserted absence is correct

capability.can reads only user.tier and returns false for an unknown capability for every tier (capability.cjs:25-31), so {tier:0} is forgeable in-process and lift() genuinely cannot succeed until master adds system.suspend-autonomy
summarise() does not carry result (:297-308), so mirroring the verdict into meta is the only way it reaches the list channel
DURABLE_STATUSES = {pending, approved} (:338) and the id is crypto.randomBytes(10).toString('hex') (:117) — /^[0-9a-f]{20}$/ is exact and the record is not a rollback source
registerApplier is appliers.set(kind, fn) on an unconstrained Map (:85) and create() accepts any kind

loyaltyGuard.PROTECTED_FILES is exactly the seven named (:64-72); inspectChanges matches by normalised equality, /-suffix or basename-plus-dirname (:220-232), so calling the guard rather than intersecting a set is required
refreshScheduler has one dispatcher: schedule()'s timer calls runNow (:204-216), runNow awaits task.run() at 133, stop() at 220 clears every timer
selfCare arms its 120s sweep at BOTH 345 and 396, kicks one at 395, runHealthSweep at 200 calls checkInstanceFailover (defined 125, invoked 224)
marketIntel: tickResolveOutcomes 731, tickSyncNews 748, timers 784-785, startScheduler/stopScheduler exported (:816)
agentOrchestrator: governor interval at 630, agent.killFn() invoked at 637 inside it; reaper-only characterisation accurate (assimilates before GC)

dependencyAdvisor.SENSITIVE is exported (:307); review() with no argument returns empty

astEngine.analyzeImpact is a substring scan (code.includes at :240, line numbers at :242) returning path.join absolutes — over-reports, never under-reports, and needs the normalisation the design specifies
localUpdateEngine.classifyChange exists and is exported (:53, :330)

House suite output is '    PASS  <msg>' / '    FAIL  <msg>' under a '\n  <id> — <title>' header (verifyInvariants.cjs:66-73)

Section 28 words I6 and I17 as the design quotes them, and Section 124's R-L4 specifies tier-0 system.suspend-autonomy, tray-reachable, unreachable by any proposal, fail-safe — the two-predicate split is an argued, printed, master-raised departure for the four pre-existing dispatchers only

unverifiedOrWrongAssumptions: WRONG: row.target on a dependencyAdvisor row — the shape is {name, pinned, latest, jump, ...} with no target (finding 2)

WRONG: 'the STOP's state is unnameable by any changes[].path' and 'the policy table is unreachable by any proposal' — timeline.cjs's SELF_MODIFY applier writes changes[].path verbatim with no root confinement, and shared/autonomy-policy.json is not in PROTECTED_FILES (finding 1)

WRONG: criterion 22a's 'startAudit() re-arms it on lift' as a description of resumption — with the stopped-record present, isHalted() stays true and three of the four dispatchers stay no-ops (finding 3)
WRONG: §B.3's nine selfModel derivations — measured eight (finding 11)
WRONG: three line citations — killFn 634, proposals.cjs 215 and 272 (finding 12)

UNVERIFIED and correctly declared by Part H, accepted as stated: nothing implemented; vite build cannot run here; the six source-change causeId recognisers have never seen real output; the vectorMemory dimension defect was found by reading; the re-key has not been run with a context domain; no Ollama daemon has ever been present so ollamaCatalog.classify is fixture-tested only; no EDITS transform has produced a byte; no timer has been observed stopping or re-arming; the 64 KB dossier cap, the 20-entry/30-day snapshot budget and the 90-day criterion window are declared budgets; requireMasterDriven's two-class carve-out is a reasoned argument no row in the document can falsify, and §I.11 is the right place for it
